title: Reproducible orchestration of best practices for reaction path optimization with the nudged elastic band1✰✰★★★★★★
author: Goswami

steps.title: Prepare consistent endpoint structures
steps.instruction: Obtain the reactant and product geometry files and ensure a one‑to‑one atom‑to‑atom mapping between them, as required for the two‑stage preparation process.

steps.title: Create YAML configuration file
steps.instruction: Write a single YAML configuration file that references the two endpoint files; this file directs the workflow to perform alignment, path generation, and optimization.

steps.title: Run workflow to generate reaction path
steps.instruction: Execute the workflow, which automatically carries out (i) geometry minimization, (ii) IRA alignment, (iii) SIDPP path generation, and (iv) hybrid CI‑NEB‑MMF optimization, without further user intervention.

substeps.instruction: Perform IRA (Iterative Rotational Alignment) of the minimized structures.
Generate an initial path using the SIDPP (String Interpolation with Discrete Path Projection) method.
Refine the path with hybrid CI‑NEB‑MMF (Climbing Image Nudged Elastic Band – Minimum Mode Following) optimization.

steps.title: Validate HCN→HNC energy profile
steps.instruction: For the HCN → HNC isomerization, compare the computed barrier of 2.46 eV and product energy of 0.57 eV above the reactant with reference CCSD(T)/cc-pCV5Z values (barrier 2.09 eV, HCN–HNC energy difference 0.65 eV) to confirm the expected single‑barrier topology.

steps.title: Apply workflow to additional systems
steps.instruction: Provide endpoint pairs for each of the four additional reactions—alanine dipeptide C7eq → C5 conformational transition, ethylene + butadiene Diels‑Alder cycloaddition, F⁻ + CH₃F SN2 identity reaction, and vinyl alcohol ↔ acetaldehyde tautomerization—then run the same workflow to obtain converged reaction paths.

description:
To demonstrate that the workflow produces correct results from raw inputs without user intervention, we apply it to the HCN → HNC isomerization, a 3-atom proton transfer with a single transition state. CCSD(T)/cc-pCV5Z calculations [17] place the barrier at 2.09 eV and the HCN–HNC energy difference at 0.65 eV. Starting from endpoint structure files alone, the workflow completes minimization, IRA alignment, SIDPP path generation, and hybrid CI-NEB-MMF optimization. The resulting energy profile (Fig. 5) recovers the expected single-barrier topology with a barrier of 2.46 eV and a product energy 0.57 eV above the reactant. The 2D (s, d) [18] landscape (Fig. 6) resolves the reactant, saddle point, and product basins.Fig. 5One-dimensional energy profile for the HCN → HNC isomerization. The single barrier of 2.46 eV separates the HCN reactant from the HNC product (0.57 eV above HCN). Colored traces show the optimization history from initial SIDPP guess (outer traces) to the converged path (black). Inset structures show the reactant, saddle point, and product geometries.Fig 5 dummy alt textFig. 6Two-dimensional RMSD landscape for the HCN → HNC isomerization. Axes represent permutation-invariant RMSD from reactant (reaction progress s) and orthogonal deviation (d). The color scale indicates interpolated energy. The reactant (R), saddle point (SP), and product (P) basins are clearly resolved.Fig 6: dummy alt text The repository includes four additional systems: the alanine dipeptide C7eq
→ C5 conformational transition, Diels-Alder cycloaddition of ethylene and butadiene, the SN2 identity reaction F- + CH3F, and vinyl alcohol to acetaldehyde tautomerization. Each requires only an endpoint pair and a YAML configuration file; the workflow handles alignment, path generation, and optimization identically. All five systems converge without manual intervention, and adding a new system amounts to providing two endpoint structures and editing a single configuration file.
